title: SolveSpace NG: the keymap pass after M3-M5
brief: One round, six questions, each picture once. Answer each row with a letter (and a note if you want it different); a complete answer is a letter on every row. Nothing is rebound yet. The doc is docs/research/keymap-pass.md; the industry comparison is docs/research/keymap-and-layout.md.

sheets.label: P1 tiers
sheets.question: P1. How often each command is used, and the key each tier gets. a = agree, b = move some (note which, to which tier).

sheets.label: P2 grammar
sheets.question: P2. The qualifier grammar: Shift = counterpart (inverse, reverse, reference), Alt = variant (same family, another shape), Ctrl = document/app, pies for big families. a = adopt it (then P3 follows), b = keep today's habit (Shift = another command on that letter, as Onshape; only P4 applies), c = other dimensions (note). My pick: a; it makes the relatives discoverable, as you asked.

sheets.label: P3 moves
sheets.question: P3. What moves if P2 is a. The big one: F becomes fillet (Fusion, Shapr3D) and the constrain pie moves to K; Shift+E becomes a new 'extrude as a cut'. a = all, b = all but some (note which), c = none.

sheets.label: P4 new keys
sheets.question: P4. Keys for what M3-M5 added: a joint pie on J, design pose on Shift+J, new part on Ctrl+Shift+N; the rarer features stay in the palette. a = yes, b = some (note), c = none.

sheets.label: P5 exceptions
sheets.question: P5. Qualified chords kept against the grammar. a = keep all six, b = hole and split curves go to the palette, c = other (note).

sheets.label: P6 letters
sheets.question: P6. Every letter after the pass with a everywhere (changes highlighted). a = build it, b = build it with the changes in your notes.
